bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, optimistic on volume growth and cost control; transparent on pricing (LME-linked, no hedging); proactive on captive resources and JV partnerships; acknowledges alumina oversupply but sees bottoming; dismisses Utkarsh JV as uneconomic
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Red mud is a future rare earth/gallium source (pilot stage); 10% of coal via E-auction despite higher cost; domestic alumina sales grew 250% YoY to 1.4LMT; special grade alumina production minimal (15-20KMT); royalty is LME-linked at 0.56% of value, not fixed
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Alumina: Production 14.46LMT (+11.5% YoY), sales 13.09LMT export, 1.37LMT domestic; Realization $348/Q4, $320/Q1FY27; Chemicals: Revenue down 12% due to $219/ton price drop, offset by volume growth; Metal: Production 4.71LMT, sales up 2.8%, realization $2,700/ton; Coal: Utkal output 4.8M tons (FY27 target), 67% captive; Power: 4.7% growth, wind up 9.25%
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Navratna CPSE with Government of India holding 51.28%; described as an 'Integrated Bauxite-Alumina-Aluminium-Power-Coal Complex'.
- Deck claims NALCO is a 'Global leader in producing bauxite and alumina at the lowest cost.'
- Asset chain spans captive bauxite mines (Damanjodi), alumina refinery (Damanjodi), aluminium smelter (Angul), captive power plant (Angul), coal, wind power and dedicated port facilities for storage of alumina, caustic soda and ship loading.
- On the demand backdrop the deck states India 'is expected to remain one of the fastest-growing Aluminium markets globally, with domestic Aluminium demand projected to grow at around 6-8% CAGR through 2030.'
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Governance] The deck lists 10 Board Level Committees but states that 'Due to absence of Independent Directors on the Board w.e.f. 01.04.2026, no Board level Committees are in position' - a live board-composition gap.
- [Governance] 'Excellent' rating in the FY25-26 self-appraisal reports to the DPE, plus 17 core policies and guidelines and regular risk assessments.
- [Price outlook] The deck's LME aluminium price outlook for CY 2026 is 'expected to average between US$ ~3200-3300/T', with global inventories at historically low levels (0.26 Mln. T) and the market 'still expected to be in deficit during the H2-2026 before gradually moving towards a more balanced position in 2027'.
- [Price drivers] Named swing factors include Middle East production/logistics disruption, moderation of the 'war-risk' premium, US tariff incentives for domestic aluminium, renewable/auto/infrastructure demand, the US$ and Fed stance, and increased Chinese (>222%) and Indonesian exports alleviating supply tightness.
- [Demand mix] Indian aluminium consumption split as given: Electrical 48%, Transportation & Automobile 15%, Building & Construction 13%, Consumer Durables 7%, Machinery & Equipments 7%, Packaging 4%, Others 6%.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Alumina cost: Rs.20k-22k/ton; Metal cost: Rs.155k-160k/ton; Key savings: 18% to 16% employee cost as % of opex (retirements > hires); Coal: Captive cost Rs.1,500/ton vs linkage Rs.1,800/ton vs E-auction Rs.2,100/ton; Caustic soda cost up to Rs.45k/ton (from Rs.42k); Power cost reduced via captive coal and wind
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth:6-8% FY27 (driven by volume); margin:EBITDA margin to hold ~48% despite alumina price pressure; order inflow:Alumina spot tenders ongoing, domestic sales target 2.5-3LMT; capex/commissioning:5th stream alumina (Jun26 comm, 2LMT output); smelter+power JV (DPR by Sep26, capex starts FY27, commissioning Dec2030)

deepdive.thesis: Despite alumina prices falling $200 YoY to $370/ton, NALCO delivered record financials due to 11.5% higher alumina production, 41.8% coal output growth, and 2.8% metal sales growth, with cost savings from captive resources and workforce rationalization offsetting commodity headwinds; the upcoming 2LMT alumina expansion and 0.5MTPA smelter with JV power plant are transformative for long-term margin resilience.

verdicts.item: Company is hopeful to produce and achieve its highest-ever annual metal production of 4,60,000 tonnes this year (FY22).
verdicts.note: expired: no update 16Q past horizon Q4FY22

verdicts.item: 5th stream refinery mechanical completion targeted by FY26 year-end (March 2026), commissioning after that and commercial production from June 2026; ~74-75% physical progress.
verdicts.note: 5th stream: mechanical work done (CWIP ~Rs.5,500 cr to capitalize), but commissioning starts June 2026 + 3-4 months, so production only 'in the last quarter' of FY27 - past the June-2026 commercial-pr…

verdicts.item: 0.5 million ton brownfield smelter DPR: consultant appointment in next 2-3 months, DPR ready for Board approval in ~7-8 months; tendering next financial year; plants likely by FY2030.
verdicts.note: DPR now to get Board approval by Sep/Oct 2026, tender 6-7 months, ordering Apr/May 2027, then ~3.5-year build; plants complete 'December 2030 or maybe early 2031' - slipped from the FY2030 target.

verdicts.item: Captive coal mines (Utkal D&E, 4 MT capacity, started Jan 2025) to complete ~4 million tons this year; no monsoon supply disruption expected due to sufficient stock.
verdicts.note: FY26 captive coal 4 MT achieved ('FY '26, we have done 4 million tons'); no monsoon disruption cited, captive ~Rs.300/ton cheaper than linkage.

verdicts.item: Existing alumina line to run above 100% of rated ~22.5 lakh ton capacity, targeting ~23 lakh tons this year (vs 20.7 lakh calcined last year).
verdicts.note: FY26 alumina production ~23 lakh tons vs 20.75 lakh in FY25 - ran above the ~22.5 lakh rated line as targeted. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: FY26 total alumina sales volume guided at around 12.5-12.8 lakh tons, with domestic sales rising to ~1-1.2 lakh tons and ~41-42 export shipments.
verdicts.note: FY26 alumina sales: '13.09 lakh tons' export + '1.37 lakh tons' domestic = ~14.46 lakh, above the 12.5-12.8 lakh guidance; domestic (~1.4 lakh) exceeded the ~1-1.2 lakh target. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: New ~1 lakh ton wire rod mill (capex ~Rs.250-300 cr) planned, DPR being revised and tendering underway; expected to take ~2 years to commission.
verdicts.note: Wire rod mill reaffirmed but capacity revised to '60,000 tons of wire rod mill... It will take around two years' (alloy-grade) - vs the earlier ~1 lakh ton plan; still in planning. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: New annealing furnace at rolled product unit coming in March 2026, lifting rolled product output from ~2,000 to ~3,000 tons per month.
verdicts.note: 'we are adding MI annealing furnace... Rolled plant on an average, we are doing around 2,000 per month. We are targeting from this year onwards around 2,500 tons per month' - output target revised dow…

verdicts.item: Aiming to sell ~80% of alumina exports on spot and ~20% on long-term contracts as long-term tender prices remain unattractive.
verdicts.note: 'most of our alumina is going on spot tenders... at present, we don't have long term because since the pricing is very low... only relying on the spot tenders' - even more spot-weighted than the ~80/2…

verdicts.item: Targeting ~10% higher volume targets across areas this year and expediting smelter+power expansion (~3-4 years) to lift turnover above Rs.25,000 cr and become a Maharatna.
verdicts.note: Best-ever FY26 physicals and smelter+power expansion being expedited (DPR order placed, 3.5-year build), but turnover Rs.17,843 cr remains below the Rs.25,000 cr Maharatna target. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: New 5th stream refinery commissioning to start June 2026, taking 3-4 months to stabilise; ~3 lakh tons of alumina production expected from it this (FY27) year, reaching full 10 lakh capacity by ~December.
verdicts.note: New-refinery FY27 alumina now '2 lakh tons' (was 3 lakh), production only in the last quarter of FY27; full 10 lakh 'next year onwards' (FY28) - ramp pushed out.

verdicts.item: FY26 alumina sales volume targeted at ~1.25-1.30 million tons (1,100 KT done in 9M); Middle East tension affected January exports, to be made up in Feb/March.
verdicts.note: FY26 alumina sales 13.09 lakh export + 1.37 lakh domestic = ~14.46 lakh (1.446 M tons) - above the ~1.25-1.30 M target despite Middle East disruption. [±10% rule]
